We got two templates. Need one that corresponds to carbonyl-ene. The first template seems weird. The second also not. We need a template that breaks alcohol and forms alkene. The first template's retro_smarts: '[C:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[CH2;D1;+0:3])-[c:4]>>O-[C@;H0;D4;+0:1](-[C:2])(-[CH3;D1;+0:3])-[c:4]'. That seems like forward: O-[C@]... -> C-C double bond. That matches carbonyl-ene? It shows product (left side) is O-[C@]... (alcohol) and reactant (right) is C-C double bond with carbonyl? Actually retro_smarts shows transformation from product to reactants? The retro_smarts is left side (product) to right side (reactants). It shows product: [C:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[CH2;D1;+0:3])-[c:4] (a carbonyl-alkene?). Wait that looks like a carbonyl (C=CH2) attached to aromatic. The right side is O-[C@]... (alcohol). So this is reverse of carbonyl-ene (i.e., breaking C-C double bond to form alcohol). That seems appropriate.

Thus we can use template_id 379649.

Now we need to apply this template to target to get precursors. Use apply_template with target SMILES and template_id 379649.
